Going to (3,5) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,6).
Going to (4,7) would cut off the bottom-right corner (10 cells). So the line goes to (6,6).

Cell (1,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,3).
Going to (2,3) would cut off the top edge (3 cells). So the line goes to (1,2).
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
